Bayesian stability of the genotypes

Source: R/decisions.R
bam_stability.Rd

bam_stability() gives the posterior distributions of two stability measures of every genotype: the AMMI stability value (ASV) of Purchase et al. (2000) computed draw by draw, and the variance of the interaction effects over the environments (Shukla's stability variance of the model), with posterior means, HPD intervals, the probability of being the most stable genotype and the posterior expected ranks, combined with the mean into a Bayesian yield stability index.

Usage

bam_stability(fit, higher_better = TRUE)

Arguments

fit

a result of bayes_ammi() or bayes_stability() (bam_stability() needs bayes_ammi()).

higher_better

TRUE (default) when larger values of the trait are better.

Value

An object of class c("bam_stability", "bam_result", "list") with stability (data.table sorted by the index: Gen, mean, ASV, ASV_lower, ASV_upper, variance, prob_most_stable (smallest ASV), rank_mean, rank_ASV, YSI). Methods: print(), plot(), bam_interpret().

Details

With the biplot scores \(u_{ik} = \lambda_k^{1/2}\alpha_{ik}\) and the sums of squares of the terms proportional to \(\lambda_k^2\), $$\mathrm{ASV}_i = \sqrt{\left(\frac{\bar{\lambda}_1^2}{\bar{\lambda}_2^2}u_{i1}\right)^2 + u_{i2}^2}, \qquad V_i = \frac{1}{E - 1}\sum_j ge_{ij}^2,$$ (\(\mathrm{ASV}_i = |u_{i1}|\) with one term), evaluated in every draw. The weight of the first axis uses the posterior means \(\bar{\lambda}_k\) of the singular values: the ratio of the draws themselves has no finite mean when the posterior of \(\lambda_2\) reaches zero. The Bayesian yield stability index is the sum of the posterior expected ranks of the mean and of the ASV.

References

Purchase, J. L., Hatting, H. and van Deventer, C. S. (2000). Genotype x environment interaction of winter wheat in South Africa: II. Stability analysis of yield performance. South African Journal of Plant and Soil, 17(3), 101–107.

Shukla, G. K. (1972). Some statistical aspects of partitioning genotype-environmental components of variability. Heredity, 29(2), 237–245. doi:10.1038/hdy.1972.87

See also

bam_superiority

Other decisions: bam_predict(), bam_ranks(), bam_superiority(), bam_winners()

Author

Muhammad Yaseen (myaseen208@gmail.com)

Examples

data(Maiz)
fit <-
  bayes_ammi(
      .data   = Maiz
    , .y      = y
    , .gen    = entry
    , .env    = site
    , .rep    = rep
    , .nIter  = 1000
    , .k      = 2
    , .burnin = 200
    , .thin   = 1
    , .chains = 1
    , .priors = bam_priors(
          mu_mean     = 0
        , mu_var      = 1e+8
        , tau_mean    = 0
        , tau_var     = 1e+8
        , delta_mean  = 0
        , delta_var   = 1e+8
        , lambda_mean = 0
        , lambda_var  = 1e+8
        , nu          = 1
        , s2          = NULL
        )
    , .level  = 0.95
    , .seed   = 1
    , .align  = TRUE
    , .model  = "AMMI"
    , .het    = FALSE
    , .waic   = TRUE
    )
st <-
  bam_stability(
      fit           = fit
    , higher_better = TRUE
    )
st$stability
